newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX volatilities well bid as dollar soars.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX volatilities well bid as dollar soars.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options were well bid in U.S. trading as the dollar rallied sharply on Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's hawkish comments, dealers said.

The dollar roared higher to above 122.50 yen and 1.69 marks, after briefly dipping back below 121 yen and 1.6750 marks initially after Greenspan's remarks, as the market began speculating on a possible Fed credit tightening.
"It was quite a dramatic reversal," said Kyoko Hiramatsu, a senior dealer at Bank of Yokohama in New York.
"Even though it seems everyone was leaning toward the short side in the last several days, they were looking for a place to get back long again," she noted.

Greenspan in his twice-yearly Humphrey-Hawkins testimony said he saw an upside risk in inflation and that he could not rule out a pre-emptive credit tightening. U.S. asset markets tumbled on the remarks, but the forex traders soon began focusing more on interest rate differentials.
"Spot had already sold off quite aggressively coming into this," said a U.S. bank trader in California, noting that the dollar might have seen an end to its corrective down move.
"We're not too far off from that old high (of 1.7050 marks in dollar/mark) now," he said. But he added that dollar/yen still had some way to go before testing highs near 125 yen.
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/mark options rose to 10.0/10.2 percent by U.S. afternoon, up half a point from late Tuesday levels and a quarter point above levels prior to Greenspan remarks.

Dollar/yen volatilities, on the other hand, were up from Tuesday but little changed from pre-Greenspan levels earlier in the day, when spot was eyeing fresh lows toward 120.50 yen. One-month rose half a point from Tuesday to 10.8/11.1 percent.

Traders said the divergent reactions of dollar/mark and dollar/yen volatilities to the dollar's rally were due partly to the weakness in the mark/yen cross, which fell below support levels above 72 yen and looked to be breaking out of a "triangle" chart pattern.
"The mark came under pressure from selling in mark/yen, and that kept dollar/mark from correcting further," Hiramatsu noted.
The California trader said one-month implied volatility for mark/yen, up 0.2 point today at 9.2/9.5 percent, was still below actual volatility of 10.2 percent.
"If spot breaks below 72 yen, vols could pick up rapidly," he said, adding that mark/yen weakness would aid dollar/mark's upward momentum.

He said the dollar/mark volatility curve was likely to be inverted for a while as the dollar tested highs, even though the premium in one-month implied volatility over actual volatility had widened to about two points today after shrinking to about one point in recent days.
